AUDIO TRANSCRIPT
ERA III
Dr. Mara Vey
First full cross-disciplinary meeting. Vey. Thorne. Kel. Vale. Orlov. Five people who, until two months ago, thought they were studying five different problems.
Crop persistence. Polymer degradation. Material failure. Atmospheric dispersal. Medical supply dependence. They're the same problem. Or parts of one.
We covered the wall in incident maps: VCF sites, hospitals, Pleroma warehouses, utility failures, atmospheric detections. The overlaps imply reservoirs we haven't identified.
Thorne called it a distributed ecosystem. Vale went silent, then asked whether anyone had complete records of international Evercrop shipments. Nobody did. I think Continuity began in that silence.

AUDIO TRANSCRIPT
ERA IV
Dr. Elias Thorne
Draft conclusion: the containment perimeter is administrative, not biological. Kel says that's too aggressive for the government brief. Vey says it isn't aggressive enough.

Orlov says if we phrase it poorly they'll stop reading. So here is the version that will never make the official report: we draw circles around visible fungus, then call everything outside the circle clean.
That is not science. That is cartography used as emotional support. Keep checkpoints. Keep decontamination. Keep slowing movement.
But stop pretending absence of visible bloom proves biological absence. It doesn't. We have enough data now to say that. I wish we didn't.
